name: Slack
look: Cream-lavender hero with pastel mesh atmospherics, one aubergine reused everywhere, and deliberately over-padded pills.

hero.title: Made for people, built for productivity
hero.sub: Channels instead of inboxes, searchable history instead of forwarded threads, and a place where the decision and the reason for it stay together.

features.title: Channels, not inboxes
features.sub: Conversation organised by topic rather than by who happened to be on the original email.

items.title: Channels
items.body: One per project or topic, open by default, so joining a team means reading rather than being briefed.

items.title: Searchable history
items.body: Every decision and the discussion around it, findable months later by anyone who joins.

items.title: Connect other companies
items.body: Shared channels with partners and customers without either side leaving their own workspace.

items.title: Huddles
items.body: Audio in a channel with one click, for the conversations that should not have been a meeting.

items.title: Workflows
items.body: Automate the routine requests — leave, access, onboarding — with a builder rather than a script.

items.title: 2,600+ apps
items.body: Your tracker, your deploys, your alerts, in the channel where the work is discussed.

showcases.title: The reason survives the decision
showcases.body: In an inbox, the reasoning behind a decision lives in someone's sent folder. In a channel, it stays next to the decision, searchable by the person who joins in eight months and asks why.
points: Searchable by anyone who joins later
Open by default, private when needed

showcases.title: Governed without being locked down
showcases.body: Retention policies, legal hold, data residency and enterprise key management — the controls a large organisation needs, without turning the tool into something people avoid using.

gallery.title: RESOURCES
gallery.sub: Guides, templates and the developer platform.

testimonial.quote: Someone joined in March and answered a question about a decision made the previous August, by searching. That is the whole value proposition and it took two minutes.
testimonial.name: Grace Chen

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free to try properly, then per active member.

items.q: What happens to messages older than 90 days on Free?
items.a: They are hidden rather than deleted, and become visible again if you upgrade. Nothing is destroyed by staying on the free plan.

items.q: Do you charge for inactive members?
items.a: No. Billing is based on members active in the period, and credit is applied automatically for anyone who was not.

items.q: Can we work with people outside the company?
items.a: Yes, through shared channels. Both sides stay in their own workspace with their own policies, which is what makes it usable across organisations.
In the region you select, with residency available on Business+ for organisations that require it contractually.

cta.title: Try it with your team
cta.sub: Free to start, and the first channel takes about a minute.

notes: A single aubergine is reused across CTAs, the featured pricing tier, the footer band and the wordmark — chromatic monotheism.
The hero canvas is cream-lavender with a diffused pastel mesh behind it, and product UI composited on top of the gradient, never inside it.
Pills carry 28–30px of horizontal padding — deliberately over-padded by SaaS-default standards.
Display sizes take tight negative tracking for editorial density.
Blue inline links are the only non-aubergine chromatic accent anywhere in body type.
